title: fix(2d): check each contour tab against every cut of its level
body:
## What changed

- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_clear.rs`. After each ring's tabs are fitted, it reads each tab's line on the ring against every other cut of the tabbed levels. The other cuts are: the other keeps of the same ring, the far part of the two keeps beside the tab, and every other ring.
- A cut nearer than the tool diameter `D` cuts into the tab. The loop is held: its tabbed levels cut nothing. A `tabs:` note names the tab and the distance.
- A cut between `D` and `W + D` away leaves the tab at its width. A `tabs:` note names the tab and the width of the strip beside it. The moves do not change.
- `tab_bridge.rs`: a `tabs:` note when the first tab grows back over a picked start. The note names the pick and the point where the tabbed levels start.
- `contour.rs`: one line. The fits of all rings are made before the level loop.
- No posted move changes for a program that gets no new note.

## Cause

The bridge check compared only the two cuts beside a tab. It read the last `W + D` of one walk and the first `W + D` of the next walk. A later run of the same ring, or a different ring, was not read.

## Shape-mask result (on upstream/main `1ae4d061f`)

Tool 6 mm, tab width 4 mm, outside contour, no leads, 0.1 mm grid.

| Case | Distance between the two cuts | Neck of the tab | Note before |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-turn, 10 mm notch | 4 mm | 0.00 mm | none |
| U-turn, 14 mm notch | 8 mm | 1.89 mm | none |
| Second ring, parts 10 mm apart | 4 mm | 0.00 mm and 0.74 mm | none |
| Second ring, parts 14 mm apart | 8 mm | 1.89 mm | none |

A bridge is narrower than the tab width, so the issue is now `P1`.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_necks.rs` (new) and `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs`:

- `a_tab_that_a_u_turn_of_its_ring_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`
- `a_tab_that_a_second_ring_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`
- `a_tab_beside_a_narrow_strip_is_named`
- `a_tab_with_room_beside_it_has_no_note`
- `the_meter_reads_the_tab_width_on_a_plain_part`
- `a_tab_that_grows_over_a_picked_start_says_so`
- `every_tabbed_level_keeps_the_tab_width` (three tabbed levels)
- `the_bridge_holds_on_the_true_arcs_to_a_tenth_of_a_micron`

Mutation results:

- Old `contour.rs` (from `upstream/main`): the U-turn pin, the second-ring pin and the strip pin are red. The meter reads necks of 0.0 mm. With the fix they are green.
- `moved_start` returns no note: `a_tab_that_grows_over_a_picked_start_says_so` is red. With the fix it is green.
- `every_tabbed_level_keeps_the_tab_width` and `the_bridge_holds_on_the_true_arcs_to_a_tenth_of_a_micron` add coverage. They are green on unchanged code too.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, 160 steps, 0 failed, 41 min. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The tab neck meter is `crates/motion/tests/common/tab_neck.rs`. `shape_mask.rs` has 409 lines, so the meter has its own file.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- `SLACK = 1e-6` did not change. A margin grows each tab window on a straight wall and moves the recorded router example program. The test reads the bridge on the posted arcs in chords of `1e-5` mm, and no bridge is under the tab width by more than `1e-4` mm. The decision file gives the bound. The reviewer can ask for the margin.
- `contour.rs` still calls `lead_held` on the first keep when that keep is not at the pick. The new note says that the start moved. A picked start with tabs permits only no lead or a perpendicular lead.
- The neck meter reads outside contours only. The inside slot and bore tests assert the hold and its note, not a neck.
- The new read uses a disc model of the tool. It can hold a loop where the true neck is still the tab width (an acute V-notch, a tab end near a tight fold). Such a hold is safe: the tabbed levels cut nothing, and a note says so.
- The check is local to the tab. It does not follow a stock strip that becomes narrow away from the tab.
- The build used no compile cache: `sccache rustc -vV` did not return on this machine. The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes these files.

## Review fixes

Commit `57756c69a` (owner-account takeover, ordered by the maintainer) fixes the two findings of the review of head `edb566d33`:

- `tab_clear::departed` reads a keep that turns back toward its tab before it is `W + D` away (a shallow notch). With one keep, its leads are read the same way. Pin: `a_tab_that_a_u_turn_in_a_shallow_notch_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`.
- `tab_clear::fit_loops` takes the tabbed levels of each loop from the depth ladder. A ring is read against a tab only when the two rings share a tabbed level. Pin: `a_ring_that_stops_above_the_tabs_does_not_hold_another_loop`.
- Quick gate on the new head: 160 steps, 0 failed. Follow-up: #2734.

Commits `3a0570587`, `97c3a445b` and `96f97f424` (owner-account takeover, ordered by the maintainer) fix the blocker of the second review (comment 7007645147):

- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_kerf.rs`. The two cuts beside a tab are also read against the core of the tab line: the line without its first and last `D / 2` (the parts that the end kerfs remove).
- A cut is skipped only while it stays in the disc of radius `D` about the tab end and goes away from the end. A cut in that disc is read against the core outside the disc. From the point where the cut leaves the disc, or turns back toward the tab end, all of the cut is read against the full core.
- A run along the tab at a constant distance is now read. A distance under `D` holds the loop with a `tabs:` note. A NaN distance holds the loop.
- `departed` stays for the "narrow strip" note. The new read can only add a hold, never a note.
- A bore or a slot that is less than about 2 x the tool diameter wide now keeps its tab-height ring of material uncut, with a `tabs:` note.

New tests in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_necks.rs`. Each test asserts that the loop is held with a `tabs:` note and cuts nothing under the tab top, or that each tab keeps the tab width:

- `a_tab_that_ends_on_the_return_run_holds_the_loop` (the review case: `notched_to(10, 15)`, start `(32, 20)`, 1 and 2 tabs)
- `a_tab_that_ends_on_the_notch_floor_or_its_corner_holds_the_loop` (start `(30, 18)` and `(32, 18)`, 1 and 2 tabs)
- `a_tab_beside_a_return_run_with_a_lead_holds_the_loop` (`Lead::Perpendicular { length: 4 }`)
- `a_tab_in_a_v_notch_keeps_its_width_or_holds_the_loop`
- `a_narrow_inside_slot_or_bore_keeps_its_tab_ring` (inside, slot 60 x 7 and bore 10, D = 6)
- `a_tab_near_a_corner_of_a_plain_part_is_not_held` (no false hold: 9 outside and 7 inside picks near one corner, 1 and 2 tabs)

Readings on the old `tab_clear.rs` (probe):

- The three tests on the return run, the floor and corner, and the lead fail. The meter reads a neck of 0.000 mm with no note, for example the tab at (25.45, 16.45) for the review case. This confirms the blocker.
- The slot, bore, V-notch and corner tests pass on the old code too. They guard against a loss and against a false hold. The 60 x 7 slot is held by the note "they fill the whole loop". The V-notch tab keeps 3.83 mm (the tab width to one cell).
- With the fix, all 13 tests of the binary pass. These suites also pass: `contour_tab_bridge` (9), `contour_tabs`, `contour_start`, `contour_whole`, `contour_auto_side`, `contour_inside_ramp`, `corner_blend_arc_contour`.
- Quick gate on head `96f97f424`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 160 steps, 0 failed, 33.1 min. No golden file and no snapshot PNG changed.
- A first draft of the fix gave a false hold on `contour_tab_bridge::a_tab_that_grows_over_a_picked_start_says_so` (15 tabs, cuts of 1.4 mm). The cause was a zero-length piece at the end mark. Commit `96f97f424` corrects it, and that test pins it.

Effort: high

Changelog: Contour tabs: a tab that another cut of the same level cuts into now holds its loop with a `tabs:` note; a narrow strip beside a tab and a start point that a tab covers get a note. A run of a cut along a tab, nearer than the tool diameter, now holds the loop too.

Fixes #2561
